Draw latent variables from an RTMB object

Source: R/rtmb-latent.R
rtmb_latent.Rd

Builds the fun of sampling() for a model whose latent variables are the random effects of an RTMB or TMB object. For each draw of the parameters from the fit, the function it returns draws the random effects from their Gaussian approximation given those parameters, so that together the draws follow the posterior of the latent variables.

Usage

rtmb_latent(obj)

Arguments

obj

An object from RTMB::MakeADFun() or TMB::MakeADFun(), built with random naming the latent variables.

Value

A function of the parameters, to pass as fun to sampling(). It returns one draw of every random effect of obj, in the object's order, named after the parameter it belongs to: u[1], u[2] and so on for a vector u.

Details

An object built with random integrates its random effects out by a Laplace approximation. Each call of obj$fn() finds their mode given the parameters, and the Hessian there is the precision of a Gaussian approximation of their distribution given the parameters. A draw is the mode plus Gaussian noise with that precision. The approximation is exact when the random effects are Gaussian given the parameters, as in a linear mixed model, and close when each has plenty of data. It is weakest for a random effect with few discrete observations: see the article "Latent variables" on the package website.

The object must return a negative log-density, as RTMB and TMB expect, and its parameters other than the random effects must be those of the fit, in the same order and on the same scale. Both hold when the fit is made from the object itself, with logpost = function(theta) -obj$fn(theta) and init = obj$par. A fit made from another function of the same model, such as a closed form with the random effects integrated out by hand, can use an object built only for this purpose.

The sparse Cholesky factor comes from the Matrix package, which RTMB and TMB install. An object's tape does not survive saveRDS(), so build the object again in a new session.

Examples

# Random intercepts u, integrated out by RTMB's Laplace approximation
set.seed(1)
group <- rep(1:8, each = 5)
y <- 2 + rnorm(8)[group] + rnorm(40, sd = 0.5)
nll <- function(p) {
  -sum(RTMB::dnorm(y, p$mu + p$u[group], exp(p$log_sigma), log = TRUE)) -
    sum(RTMB::dnorm(p$u, 0, exp(p$log_tau), log = TRUE)) -
    RTMB::dnorm(p$mu, 0, 10, log = TRUE) -
    RTMB::dnorm(p$log_tau, 0, 2, log = TRUE) -
    RTMB::dnorm(p$log_sigma, 0, 2, log = TRUE)
}
obj <- RTMB::MakeADFun(
  nll,
  list(mu = 0, log_tau = 0, log_sigma = 0, u = numeric(8)),
  random = "u",
  silent = TRUE
)
fit <- inla_vanilla(
  function(theta) -obj$fn(theta),
  obj$par,
  grad = function(theta) -as.vector(obj$gr(theta)),
  silent = TRUE
)

# One row per draw of the parameters, one column per random intercept
u <- sampling(fit, nsamp = 500, fun = rtmb_latent(obj))
round(colMeans(u), 2)
#>  u[1]  u[2]  u[3]  u[4]  u[5]  u[6]  u[7]  u[8] 
#> -0.61 -0.01 -0.65  1.06  0.29 -1.14  0.50  0.56
